key_insight: A data-driven framework that uses skeleton-based biomechanical analysis and motion modeling to capture whole-body coordination and release dynamics enables personalized, actionable darts training beyond single-metric or static-template approaches.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between experience-based coaching and limited quantitative methods by providing holistic, individualized assessment and feedback for high-precision dart throwing.
method: Extract skeleton and joint kinematics from video/sensor data to quantify temporal biomechanics (joint angles, velocities, coordination).
Model throwing sequences and release parameters with temporal/machine-learning motion models to capture typical patterns and failure modes.
Personalize guidance by comparing an individual's motion to learned prototypes or personalized baselines and generating targeted corrective suggestions.
impact: Demonstrates how pose estimation + time-series modeling can produce individualized, interpretable training feedback—useful for ML practitioners building real-world human-motion applications and personalized coaching systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side video frames with skeleton overlay showing joint angles at key phases (preparation, release, follow-through).
Time-series plots of joint trajectories and release parameters with highlighted deviations from an ideal or personal baseline.
Player-style clustering map (2D embedding) showing prototypes and recommended drills per cluster.
Compact corrective-action icons linked to specific biomechanical errors (e.g., elbow angle, wrist timing) with expected outcome improvements.
paper_title: Toward Personalized Darts Training: A Data-Driven Framework Based on Skeleton-Based Biomechanical Analysis and Motion Modeling
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Dongyi He, Jin Fang, Xi Chen, Yisuo Liu
